import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.44

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

A union $\mathfrak A = \bigcup_\alpha \mathfrak V_\alpha$ of varieties of groups, where
union means join in the lattice of varieties, is called irreducible if
$\bigcup_{\beta \ne \alpha} \mathfrak V_\beta \ne \mathfrak A$ for every $\alpha$.
Is every variety an irreducible union of finitely or infinitely many varieties, each of which
cannot be decomposed into a union of two proper subvarieties?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.44»

/-- A group law in countably many variables, written as a word required to equal one. -/
abbrev GroupLaw := FreeGroup ℕ

/-- The group $G$ satisfies the law $w$ if every assignment of its variables in $G$
makes $w$ equal to one. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type) [Group G] (w : GroupLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The semantic consequences, in the theory of groups, of a set of group laws. -/
def consequence (S : Set GroupLaw) : Set GroupLaw :=
  {w | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], S ⊆ {v | SatisfiesLaw G v} → SatisfiesLaw G w}

/-- Semantic consequence is a closure operator on sets of group laws. -/
def groupLawClosure : ClosureOperator (Set GroupLaw) where
  toFun := consequence
  monotone' S T hST w hw G _ hGT := hw G (hST.trans hGT)
  le_closure' S w hw G _ hGS := hGS hw
  idempotent' S := Set.Subset.antisymm
    (fun w hw G _ hGS ↦ hw G fun v hv ↦ hv G hGS)
    (fun w hw G _ hGcS ↦ hGcS hw)

noncomputable instance : CompleteLattice groupLawClosure.Closeds :=
  groupLawClosure.gi.liftCompleteLattice

/-- A variety of groups, represented by its semantically closed theory of identities.
The order is dual to inclusion of theories, and hence agrees with inclusion of the
corresponding classes of groups. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := (groupLawClosure.Closeds)ᵒᵈ

/-- A lattice element cannot be expressed as the join of two proper elements. This definition
includes the bottom element, which has no proper subvarieties. -/
def IsJoinIndecomposable {L : Type*} [Lattice L] (V : L) : Prop :=
  ∀ V₁ V₂, V₁ < V → V₂ < V → V₁ ⊔ V₂ ≠ V

/--
Is every variety an irreducible union of finitely or infinitely many varieties, each of which
cannot be decomposed into a union of two proper subvarieties?

Here joins are unions in the lattice of varieties. Irreducibility means that deleting any
one member of the indexed family changes its join.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.44» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A : GroupVariety, ∃ (ι : Type) (V : ι → GroupVariety),
      (∀ i, IsJoinIndecomposable (V i)) ∧
      (⨆ i, V i) = A ∧
      ∀ i, (⨆ (j) (_ : j ≠ i), V j) ≠ A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.44»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.44

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

A union $\mathfrak{A} = \bigcup_{\alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\alpha}$ of varieties of groups (in the
lattice of varieties) is called *irreducible* if
$\bigcup_{\beta \ne \alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\beta} \ne \mathfrak{A}$ for each index $\alpha$.
Is every variety an irreducible union of (finitely or infinitely many) varieties each of which
cannot be decomposed into a union of two proper subvarieties?

A *variety of groups* is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and
arbitrary (Cartesian) direct products; by Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of
groups defined by sets of laws. Varieties are ordered by inclusion and form a complete lattice.
The *union* of a family of varieties is its join in this lattice, i.e. the smallest variety
containing every member of the family (in general strictly larger than the set-theoretic union of
the classes).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.44»

universe u

/-- A variety of groups (with groups taken in the universe `Type u`): a class of groups that is
closed under subgroups (more precisely, under isomorphic copies of subgroups), homomorphic images
and arbitrary direct products. The empty product is the trivial group, so every variety contains
the trivial groups. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The class of groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- Varieties are closed under subgroups (and isomorphic copies). -/
  mem_of_injective : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Injective f → Mem H → Mem G
  /-- Varieties are closed under homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Surjective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- Varieties are closed under arbitrary direct products. -/
  mem_pi : ∀ {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, Mem (G i)) → Mem (∀ i, G i)

namespace GroupVariety

variable {V W : GroupVariety.{u}}

@[ext, category API, AMS 20]
theorem ext (h : ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Mem G ↔ W.Mem G) : V = W := by
  obtain ⟨V, _, _, _⟩ := V
  obtain ⟨W, _, _, _⟩ := W
  congr
  funext G inst
  exact propext (h G)

/-- Varieties are ordered by inclusion of the underlying classes of groups. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety.{u} where
  le V W := ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ h := h
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ h := h₂ G (h₁ G h)
  le_antisymm _ _ h₁ h₂ := ext fun G _ => ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_def : V ≤ W ↔ ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G := Iff.rfl

/-- The intersection of any set of varieties is a variety. -/
instance : InfSet GroupVariety.{u} where
  sInf s :=
    { Mem := fun G _ => ∀ V ∈ s, V.Mem G
      mem_of_injective := fun f hf h V hV => V.mem_of_injective f hf (h V hV)
      mem_of_surjective := fun f hf h V hV => V.mem_of_surjective f hf (h V hV)
      mem_pi := fun h V hV => V.mem_pi fun i => h i V hV }

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_sInf {s : Set GroupVariety.{u}} {G : Type u} [Group G] :
    (sInf s).Mem G ↔ ∀ V ∈ s, V.Mem G := Iff.rfl

/-- The lattice of varieties of groups. Meets are intersections of classes; the union (join) of a
family of varieties is the smallest variety containing all of its members. -/
instance : CompleteLattice GroupVariety.{u} :=
  completeLatticeOfInf GroupVariety.{u} fun _ =>
    ⟨fun _ hV _ _ h => h _ hV, fun _ hW _ _ hG _ hV => hW hV _ hG⟩

/-- A variety `V` is *indecomposable* if it cannot be decomposed into a union of two proper
subvarieties, i.e. `V₁ ⊔ V₂ ≠ V` whenever `V₁ < V` and `V₂ < V`. This includes the
trivial variety `⊥`, which has no proper subvarieties at all (in contrast to Mathlib's
`SupIrred`, which excludes the bottom element). -/
def IsIndecomposable (V : GroupVariety.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ V₁ V₂ : GroupVariety.{u}, V₁ < V → V₂ < V → V₁ ⊔ V₂ ≠ V

/-- A family `V : ι → GroupVariety` of varieties is an *irreducible union* of the variety `A` if
$\bigcup_{\alpha} V_{\alpha} = A$ while $\bigcup_{\beta \ne \alpha} V_{\beta} \ne A$ for each
index $\alpha$, where $\bigcup$ denotes the union (join) in the lattice of varieties. -/
def IsIrreducibleUnion {ι : Type*} (V : ι → GroupVariety.{u}) (A : GroupVariety.{u}) : Prop :=
  (⨆ α, V α) = A ∧ ∀ α, (⨆ β ≠ α, V β) ≠ A

/-- The class of all groups is a variety; it is the top of the lattice of varieties. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mem_top (G : Type u) [Group G] : (⊤ : GroupVariety.{u}).Mem G :=
  fun _ h => h.elim

/-- The trivial variety, consisting of the trivial groups. -/
def trivial : GroupVariety.{u} where
  Mem G _ := Subsingleton G
  mem_of_injective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_of_surjective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_pi _ := inferInstance

/-- The abelian groups form a variety. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem exists_mem_iff_isMulCommutative :
    ∃ V : GroupVariety.{u}, ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Mem G ↔ IsMulCommutative G :=
  ⟨{ Mem := fun G _ => IsMulCommutative G
     mem_of_injective := fun _ hf h =>
       ⟨⟨fun a b => hf (by rw [map_mul, map_mul, h.is_comm.comm])⟩⟩
     mem_of_surjective := fun f hf h => ⟨⟨fun a b => by
       obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hf a
       obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hf b
       rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul, h.is_comm.comm]⟩⟩
     mem_pi := fun h => ⟨⟨fun a b => funext fun i => (h i).is_comm.comm (a i) (b i)⟩⟩ },
    fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩

/-- Every variety contains the trivial groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_of_subsingleton (V : GroupVariety.{u}) (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    V.Mem G :=
  V.mem_of_injective (1 : G →* (∀ _ : PEmpty.{u + 1}, PUnit.{u + 1}))
    (fun a b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b) (V.mem_pi fun i => i.elim)

/-- The trivial variety is the bottom of the lattice of varieties. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem trivial_eq_bot : (trivial : GroupVariety.{u}) = ⊥ := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (fun G _ h => h trivial (Set.mem_univ _))
  intro G _ h V _
  haveI : Subsingleton G := h
  exact V.mem_of_subsingleton G

/-- The trivial variety is indecomposable, since it has no proper subvarieties. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isIndecomposable_bot : IsIndecomposable (⊥ : GroupVariety.{u}) :=
  fun _ _ h _ _ => not_lt_bot h

/-- The trivial variety is the irreducible union of the empty family. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isIrreducibleUnion_empty :
    IsIrreducibleUnion (fun x : Empty => x.elim) (⊥ : GroupVariety.{u}) :=
  ⟨iSup_of_empty _, fun x => x.elim⟩

end GroupVariety

open GroupVariety

/--
A union $\mathfrak{A} = \bigcup_{\alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\alpha}$ of varieties of groups (in the
lattice of varieties) is called *irreducible* if
$\bigcup_{\beta \ne \alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\beta} \ne \mathfrak{A}$ for each index $\alpha$.

Here "union" is the join in the lattice of varieties. The family
$(\mathfrak{V}_{\alpha})_{\alpha \in \iota}$ may be indexed by any type `ι : Type`; irreducibility
forces $\alpha \mapsto \mathfrak{V}_{\alpha}$ to be injective, so this covers families of every
cardinality. The family may be empty; the empty family is the only irreducible decomposition of
the trivial variety.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.44» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A : GroupVariety.{0}, ∃ (ι : Type) (V : ι → GroupVariety.{0}),
      (∀ α, IsIndecomposable (V α)) ∧ IsIrreducibleUnion V A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.44»

namespace Kourovka.«5.44»

/-- A group law in countably many variables, written as a word required to equal one. -/
abbrev GroupLaw := FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies a law `w` if every assignment of its variables in `G` evaluates `w`
to one. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type) [Group G] (w : GroupLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A group `G` models a set `T` of group laws if it satisfies every law in `T`. -/
def Models (G : Type) [Group G] (T : Set GroupLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃w⦄, w ∈ T → SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A set of group laws represents a variety of groups when it contains exactly all laws that
hold in all of its models. Thus varieties are identified when they have the same laws. -/
def IsGroupVariety (T : Set GroupLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ T ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Models G T → SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- In the representation by sets of laws, the join of varieties is the intersection of their
law sets. This says that `V` cannot be expressed as the join of two proper subvarieties. -/
def IsJoinIrreducible (V : Set GroupLaw) : Prop :=
  IsGroupVariety V ∧ ∀ U W, IsGroupVariety U → IsGroupVariety W →
    U ∩ W = V → U = V ∨ W = V

/--
Is every variety an irreducible join of finitely or infinitely many varieties that cannot be
decomposed as a join of two proper subvarieties?

Varieties are represented by their semantically closed sets of laws. Under this representation,
a lattice join is the intersection of law sets. Hence `⋂ β, ⋂ (_ : β ≠ α), V β` is the join
with the term indexed by `α` omitted.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.44» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A, IsGroupVariety A →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (V : ι → Set GroupLaw),
        (∀ α, IsJoinIrreducible (V α)) ∧
        (⋂ α, V α) = A ∧
        ∀ α, (⋂ β, ⋂ (_ : β ≠ α), V β) ≠ A := by

Under the law-set representation, inclusion of varieties reverses inclusion of law sets, so arbitrary lattice joins are represented by intersections.
Expressed omission of the α-indexed component as `⋂ β, ⋂ (_ : β ≠ α), V β`; this also gives the intended universal law set for an empty remaining family.

Edge case: the trivial variety ⊥ is the irreducible union of the empty set S = ∅ (sSup ∅ = ⊥), so the statement is harmlessly true for A = ⊥; with S = {⊥} irreducibility would fail, so the empty family must be allowed (as the notes say).

new_definitions.why_needed: Varieties of groups (and their lattice) are absent from Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined as a class of groups in `Type u` (predicate `Mem : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop`) closed under homomorphic images (surjective homs), subgroups (injective homs) and arbitrary direct products (`∀ i, G i` over `ι : Type u`). statement_blocks.kourovka.«5.44»:
/--
A union $\mathfrak{A} = \bigcup_{\alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\alpha}$ of varieties of groups (in the
lattice of varieties) is called *irreducible* if
$\bigcup_{\beta \ne \alpha} \mathfrak{V}_{\beta} \ne \mathfrak{A}$ for each index $\alpha$.
Is every variety an irreducible union of (finitely or infinitely many) varieties each of which
cannot be decomposed into a union of two proper subvarieties?

Here "union" is the join in the lattice of varieties. An irreducible union is necessarily
injectively indexed (repeating a member would make it redundant), so the family
$(\mathfrak{V}_{\alpha})_{\alpha}$ is represented by the set $S$ of its members; the union over
all $\beta \ne \alpha$ is then `sSup (S \ {V})`. A variety $\mathfrak{V}$ "cannot be decomposed
into a union of two proper subvarieties" if there are no $\mathfrak{V}_1, \mathfrak{V}_2
\subsetneq \mathfrak{V}$ with $\mathfrak{V}_1 \cup \mathfrak{V}_2 = \mathfrak{V}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.44» : answer(sorry) ↔

      sSup S = A ∧ (∀ V ∈ S, sSup (S \ {V}) ≠ A) ∧
      ∀ V ∈ S, ¬ ∃ V₁ V₂, V₁ < V ∧ V₂ < V ∧ V₁ ⊔ V₂ = V := by
